2607.15218.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
2607.15218.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as high-level planners for embodied agents, where linguistically benign instructions can become unsafe once grounded in the physical world. We study whether this physically grounded danger is the same safety problem as ordinary text-level content danger. Through hidden-state direction analysis and random-split null tests, we show that content danger (CD) and physical danger (PD) form separable signals in LLM representations across Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B, Phi-3.5 and SmolLM2. Building on the CD/PD separability, we propose PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states. PRISM achieves 86.2--87.7\% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7--13.7\% FPR, while same-scale LLM judges over-block safe tasks at 24.7--39.0\% FPR. We further introduce PhysicalSafetyBench-1K (PSB-1K), a contrastive benchmark of 1{,}000 physical-risk pairs without direct harm keywords, to test whether methods detect physically grounded danger rather than explicit unsafe wording. On PSB-1K, PRISM reaches 99.6\% accuracy and 0.7\% FPR, whereas a Qwen2.5-3B judge rejects 67.8\% of safe tasks. PRISM also replicates on SafeText and EARBench, supporting hidden-state probing as a representation-level method for physical safety beyond text moderation.
2607.15218.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地作為具身代理的高階規劃者，其中語言上無害的指令在實體世界中可能變得不安全。我們研究這種物理基礎的危險是否與普通文本層級內容的危險是相同的安全問題。通過隱藏狀態方向分析和隨機拆分的虛無測試，我們顯示內容危險（CD）和物理危險（PD）在Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B、Phi-3.5和SmolLM2的LLM表示中形成可分離的信號。基於CD/PD的可分離性，我們提出了PRISM，一個對完整隱藏狀態進行單層L2正則化邏輯探測的模型。PRISM在SafeAgentBench上達到了86.2--87.7\%的準確率，並且FPR為11.7--13.7\%，而同規模的LLM在過度阻止安全任務時的FPR為24.7--39.0\%。我們進一步介紹了PhysicalSafetyBench-1K（PSB-1K），這是一個包含1,000個物理風險對的對比基準，沒有直接的傷害關鍵詞，以測試方法是否檢測到物理基礎的危險，而不是明確的不安全措辭。在PSB-1K上，PRISM達到了99.6\%的準確率和0.7\%的FPR，而Qwen2.5-3B的評估者拒絕了67.8\%的安全任務。PRISM在SafeText和EARBench上也能重現，支持隱藏狀態探測作為超越文本審核的物理安全表示層級方法。
